biological_question: Within original Petunieae taxa sharing an identical anthocyanidin six-bit presence class, does the original fixed four-gene flavonol-related expression profile improve out-of-species prediction of the *three measured flavonol concentrations* beyond the pigment-class mean?
previously_exposed_biology: Original gene-module source-prediction outcome +5.6137% for F3primeH/FLS/MYBFL/MYB12, measured flavonol amount k2-from-tree practical FAIL -24.0803%. This is a new target-vs-expression association and is source-exposed retrospective, not external blind validation.

fixed_frame.source_units: expression log1p(original TPM10K), metabolites log1p(100 * original mg/g)

primary_model.test: 47 species leave-one-out crossvalidated prediction within original source
primary_model.baseline: For each omitted species i, take mean of measured flavonol transformed target vector Y among the other original species carrying the same fixed anthocyanidin-presence class
primary_model.candidate: Add the four fixed measured expression predictors through a shared-slope ridge regression, with unpenalized fixed intercept per six-bit pigment class. In each heldout fold, z-standardize each gene using only other 46 tips, centre standardized gene features and Y within training pigment class, and fit B=solve(X_center.T@X_center + alpha I, X_center.T@Y_center). Predict heldout Y as training-only class mean of Y plus target deviation from the training-only same-class predictor mean times B.
primary_model.alpha_scale: Ridge alpha in coordinates z-scored using only the 46 training gene values, applied to all four gene coefficient columns, no penalty on six fixed source class intercepts
primary_model.donor_condition: Measured expression of held-out taxon is available; exact pigment state of target already known; not a prediction from DNA or a mechanistic perturbation
primary_model.loss: mean of 3 compound per species squared errors / corresponding target variance from its other 46 source taxa (population ddof0); then equal average over 47 heldout species
primary_model.gain: (class-mean LOOCV MSE - gene+class ridge LOOCV MSE)/class-mean LOOCV MSE. Positive means additional predictive information in gene expression beyond source class
primary_model.rule: SUPPORTED_RETROSPECTIVE_WITHIN_SOURCE_EXPRESSION_TO_PRODUCT_TRANSFER if observed gain > 0 AND positive-tail within-class whole-vector permutation P<=0.05; otherwise NOT_SUPPORTED. This is NOT a causal gene-to-metabolite statement.
primary_model.phylogeny_robustness_caveat: Same-tree taxa and source class fixed, but correlations due to shared ancestry/environment may drive outcome. This model only tests conditional predictive association; no causal or phylogenetic mixed-effect proof.

permutation.exchangeability: Randomly permute the intact *four-gene source vector* among the 47 taxa strictly within the six original fine anthocyanidin-presence classes while holding measured Y values and class assignments fixed. Redo all leave-one-species-out train-standardized ridge predictions. This retains within-gene correlation and source class effects but is NOT a null that preserves within-class phylogenetic expression autocorrelation.
permutation.p_value: one-sided upper-tail (1 + number null gains >= observed gain)/10000

secondary_descriptive.per_original_class: Report per-class baseline and ridge error/gain for all six fixed original class labels; no class rescues
secondary_descriptive.per_target: Report myricetin, quercetin and kaempferol individual prediction gains as descriptive only without extra P values
secondary_descriptive.training_scaling_and_expression: Compute training-only gene means, gene variances, and measured-product variances in each held-out fold
secondary_descriptive.alpha_sensitivity_note: Alpha 1 and 100 are post-result descriptive robustness; no new p values or selection of best alpha
secondary_descriptive.paired_tip_breadth: Count 47 recipients improved or worse; source descriptive only
